title_en: Law of the People's Republic of China on the Application of Laws to Foreign-Related Civil Relations

articles.content_en: Article 1 This Law is enacted for the purpose of clarifying the application of laws to civil relations involving foreign elements, reasonably resolving civil disputes involving foreign elements, and safeguarding the lawful rights and interests of parties.

Article 2 The laws applicable to civil relations involving foreign elements shall be determined in accordance with this Law. Where other laws provide otherwise specially for the application of laws to civil relations involving foreign elements, such provisions shall prevail.
Where neither this Law nor any other law provides for the application of laws to a civil relation involving foreign elements, the law having the closest connection with such civil relation shall apply.
Article 3 The parties may, in accordance with the provisions of laws, expressly choose the law applicable to a civil relation involving foreign elements.
Article 4 Where a mandatory provision of the law of the People's Republic of China applies to a civil relation involving foreign elements, such mandatory provision shall be directly applied.
Article 5 Where the application of a foreign law would impair the social public interests of the People's Republic of China, the law of the People's Republic of China shall apply.

Article 6 Where a foreign law is applicable to a civil relation involving foreign elements, and different regions of that country implement different laws, the law of the region having the closest connection with such civil relation shall apply.
Article 7 The limitation of action shall be governed by the law applicable to the relevant civil relation involving foreign elements.
Article 8 The characterization of a civil relation involving foreign elements shall be governed by the law of the forum.
Article 9 The foreign law applicable to a civil relation involving foreign elements shall not include the conflict-of-laws rules of that country.

Article 10 The foreign law applicable to a civil relation involving foreign elements shall be ascertained by the People's Court, arbitral institution, or administrative organ. Where the parties choose to apply a foreign law, they shall provide the law of that country.
Where it is impossible to ascertain the foreign law or such country has no relevant provision, the law of the People's Republic of China shall apply.
Article 11 The capacity of a natural person for civil rights shall be governed by the law of his habitual residence.

Article 12 The capacity of a natural person for civil conduct shall be governed by the law of his habitual residence.
Where a natural person engaging in civil activities is considered to have no capacity for civil conduct under the law of his habitual residence but is considered to have capacity for civil conduct under the law of the place where the act is performed, the law of the place where the act is performed shall apply, except for matters involving marriage, family, or succession.
Article 13 A declaration of missing person or death shall be governed by the law of the natural person's habitual residence.

Article 14 Matters such as the capacity for civil rights, capacity for civil conduct, organizational structure, and rights and obligations of shareholders of a legal person and its branches shall be governed by the law of the place of registration.
Where the principal place of business of a legal person is inconsistent with the place of registration, the law of the principal place of business may apply. The habitual residence of a legal person shall be its principal place of business.
Article 15 The content of personality rights shall be governed by the law of the habitual residence of the right holder.

Article 16 Agency shall be governed by the law of the place where the agency act is performed, except that the civil relationship between the principal and the agent shall be governed by the law of the place where the agency relationship arises.
The parties may by agreement choose the law applicable to a mandate agency.

Article 17 The parties may by agreement choose the law applicable to a trust. Where the parties have made no choice, the law of the place where the trust property is located or the law of the place where the trust relationship arises shall apply.

Article 18 The parties may by agreement choose the law applicable to an arbitration agreement. Where the parties have made no choice, the law of the place where the arbitral institution is located or the law of the place of arbitration shall apply.

Article 19 Where the law of the state of nationality is applicable in accordance with this Law, and a natural person has two or more nationalities, the law of the state of nationality in which he has habitual residence shall apply; if he has no habitual residence in any state of nationality, the law of the state of nationality having the closest connection with him shall apply. Where a natural person is stateless or of uncertain nationality, the law of his habitual residence shall apply.
Article 20 Where the law of habitual residence is applicable in accordance with this Law, if the habitual residence of a natural person is uncertain, the law of his present residence shall apply.

Article 21 The conditions for marriage shall be governed by the law of the common habitual residence of the parties; in the absence of a common habitual residence, the law of their common nationality shall apply; in the absence of a common nationality, if the marriage is concluded in the habitual residence or the state of nationality of one party, the law of the place of marriage conclusion shall apply.

Article 22 A marriage shall be valid as to its form if it complies with the law of the place of its conclusion, the law of the habitual residence of either party, or the law of the state of nationality of either party.

Article 23 The personal relationship between spouses shall be governed by the law of their common habitual residence; in the absence of a common habitual residence, the law of their common nationality shall apply.

Article 24 As to the property relationship between spouses, the parties may by agreement choose the law of the habitual residence of either party, the law of the state of nationality of either party, or the law of the place where the main property is located. Where the parties have made no choice, the law of their common habitual residence shall apply; in the absence of a common habitual residence, the law of their common nationality shall apply.

Article 25 The personal and property relationships between parents and children shall be governed by the law of their common habitual residence; in the absence of a common habitual residence, the law of the habitual residence of either party or the law of the state of nationality of either party that is more favorable to protecting the rights and interests of the weaker party shall apply.

Article 26 For divorce by agreement, the parties may by agreement choose the law of the habitual residence of either party or the law of the state of nationality of either party. Where the parties have made no choice, the law of their common habitual residence shall apply; in the absence of a common habitual residence, the law of their common nationality shall apply; in the absence of a common nationality, the law of the place where the authority handling the divorce is located shall apply.
Article 27 Divorce by litigation shall be governed by the law of the forum.

Article 28 The conditions and formalities for adoption shall be governed by the law of the habitual residence of the adopter and the adoptee. The effects of adoption shall be governed by the law of the habitual residence of the adopter at the time of adoption. The dissolution of an adoptive relationship shall be governed by the law of the habitual residence of the adoptee at the time of adoption or the law of the forum.

Article 29 Maintenance shall be governed by the law of the habitual residence of either party, the law of the state of nationality of either party, or the law of the place where the main property is located, whichever is more favorable to protecting the rights and interests of the maintenance recipient.

Article 30 Guardianship shall be governed by the law of the habitual residence of either party or the law of the state of nationality of either party, whichever is more favorable to protecting the rights and interests of the ward.

Article 31 Statutory succession shall be governed by the law of the decedent's habitual residence at the time of his death; however, statutory succession of immovable property shall be governed by the law of the place where such property is located.

Article 32 A will shall be valid as to its form if it complies with the law of the habitual residence of the testator at the time of making the will or at the time of his death, the law of the state of his nationality, or the law of the place where the will was made.

Article 33 The validity of a will shall be governed by the law of the habitual residence of the testator at the time of making the will or at the time of his death, or the law of the state of his nationality.
Article 34 Matters such as the administration of an estate shall be governed by the law of the place where the estate is located.
Article 35 The ownership of an estate without a successor shall be governed by the law of the place where the estate is located at the time of the decedent's death.
Article 36 Real rights in immovable property shall be governed by the law of the place where such property is located.

Article 37 The parties may by agreement choose the law applicable to real rights in movable property. Where the parties have made no choice, the law of the place where the movable property is located at the time when the legal fact occurs shall apply.

Article 38 The parties may by agreement choose the law applicable to the change of real rights in movable property in transit. Where the parties have made no choice, the law of the place of destination shall apply.
Article 39 Negotiable securities shall be governed by the law of the place where the rights under such securities are realized or the law having the closest connection with such securities.
Article 40 A pledge of rights shall be governed by the law of the place where such pledge is created.

Article 41 The parties may by agreement choose the law applicable to a contract. Where the parties have made no choice, the law of the habitual residence of the party whose performance of obligations best reflects the characteristics of the contract, or the law having the closest connection with the contract, shall apply.

Article 42 A consumer contract shall be governed by the law of the consumer's habitual residence; if the consumer chooses to apply the law of the place where the goods or services are provided, or if the business operator does not engage in relevant business activities in the consumer's habitual residence, the law of the place where the goods or services are provided shall apply.

Article 43 A labor contract shall be governed by the law of the place where the worker performs his work; if the place where the worker performs his work is difficult to determine, the law of the principal place of business of the employer shall apply. For labor dispatch, the law of the place where the dispatch occurs may apply.

Article 44 Tort liability shall be governed by the law of the place where the tortious act is committed; however, if the parties have a common habitual residence, the law of their common habitual residence shall apply. Where the parties agree on the applicable law after the occurrence of the tortious act, their agreement shall prevail.

Article 45 Product liability shall be governed by the law of the habitual residence of the injured party; if the injured party chooses to apply the law of the principal place of business of the tortfeasor or the law of the place where the damage occurred, or if the tortfeasor does not engage in relevant business activities in the habitual residence of the injured party, the law of the principal place of business of the tortfeasor or the law of the place where the damage occurred shall apply.

Article 46 Where personality rights such as the right to name, right to portrait, right to reputation, or right to privacy are infringed upon through the Internet or by other means, the law of the habitual residence of the injured party shall apply.

Article 47 For unjust enrichment or negotiorum gestio, the law chosen by agreement of the parties shall apply. Where the parties have made no choice, the law of their common habitual residence shall apply; in the absence of a common habitual residence, the law of the place where the unjust enrichment or negotiorum gestio occurs shall apply.
Article 48 The ownership and content of intellectual property rights shall be governed by the law of the place where protection is claimed.

Article 49 The parties may by agreement choose the law applicable to the transfer and licensing of intellectual property rights. Where the parties have made no choice, the relevant provisions of this Law on contracts shall apply.

Article 50 Tort liability for infringement of intellectual property rights shall be governed by the law of the place where protection is claimed; the parties may also, after the occurrence of the infringement, by agreement choose to apply the law of the forum.

Article 51 If the provisions of Article 146 and Article 147 of the General Principles of the Civil Law of the People's Republic of China, and Article 36 of the Succession Law of the People's Republic of China are inconsistent with the provisions of this Law, this Law shall apply.
Article 52 This Law shall come into force as of April 1, 2011.
